thread:
incident-bot: [PAGER] P2 \u2014 model-runner (eu-west-1) worker-cpu-throttled > 90% for 5m. Paging oncall: @nora. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-runner-cpu INC-7890

nora: ack. pulling cpu/memory + pod events. any recent config or autoscaler changes?

ethan: no infra deploys. saw sustained high CPU from a set of pods handling long-context requests. requests per-second steady, but per-request work jumped.

zara: looks like a new customer test job hit staging->prod tag by mistake at 22:10 UTC, high token counts (10k tokens) causing prolonged CPU.

nora: immediate mitigation: 1) create short maintenance window to suppress noisy paging while we triage, 2) apply emergency rate-limit on model-runner ingress to cap tokens/request to 2048, 3) scale up extra workers to drain backlog.

oncall-bot: handoff note: next oncall @leo in 30m (23:20 UTC). current assignee: @nora.

nora: creating 1h maintenance window: MW-3301 for eu-west-1 model-runner. will also create a 90m silence for cpu-throttled alert. Silence ID: S-1984.

infra: scaled +4 replicas for deployment/model-runner-prod-eu. scaling observed, new pods in ready state in ~2m.

ethan: applying token cap via ingress filter: 
```
POST /ingress/rate-limit
{
  "service":"model-runner",
  "max_tokens_per_request":2048
}
```
applied. backlog draining. CPU throttled dropped from 92% -> 47% within 4m.

zara: good. customer test aborted. real user impact minimal but alerts noisy during mitigation.

observability-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: CPU throttling reduced; continuing to monitor for 15m prior to resolution.

nora: moving to post-incident work: this incident showed our 90% cpu-throttled alert is too sensitive to short bursts caused by large single requests. proposals: 
- change firing rule: require cpu_throttled > 90% for 5m AND running_avg_tokens_per_req > 3000 for 2m
- add absolute backlog threshold: queue_length > 50 sustained for 3m to indicate system pressure
- create a dashboard panel for requests-by-token-count histogram and recent maintenance windows/active silences
- add a runbook snippet for emergency ingress token cap and quick autoscale knobs

ethan: +1. also propose adding a label to alerts when a maintenance window or scheduled job is present (alerts include label maintenance=true). avoids noisy pages for expected jobs.

zara: we should validate threshold changes against last 30 days; night windows have heavy batch workloads. suggest replay: tools/alert_replay.py --alert model_cpu_throttle --duration 30d --extra-metrics tokens_per_req,queue_length

leo: quick thought: instead of static token cap, add a temporary dynamic limiter that scales with available CPU headroom. will prototype but need observability metrics wired to enable it safely.

nora: action plan I'll own:
1) open observability PR to update alert rule (threshold + token filter + backlog rule)
2) add histogram panel + maintenance/silence annotation to Grafana
3) create runbook snippet and a one-click ingress cap job in the playbook UI
4) run alert_replay + synthetic test with long-token requests in staging

observability-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/observability/pull/934 \u2014 draft changes: add token-rate predicate to model_cpu_throttle, new alert model_queue_high, annotate alerts with maintenance flag.

ethan: I'll run the replay script and post results here. starting replay for 30d...

ethan: replay complete. with new rule, 7 potential fires over 30d, all correlated with scheduled GV bulk jobs (nightly). current 90%-only rule would have fired 42 times.

zara: good signal-to-noise improvement. for the 7 correlated cases, they align with batch windows so they should be suppressed by maintenance windows.

nora: creating ticket TKT-6122: ensure scheduled bulk jobs register maintenance windows and include metadata `scheduled_job=true` so alerts can suppress.

leo: for synthetic, I'll run a long-token load in staging for 30m and verify alert triggers only when backlog grows and token rate high.

leo: synthetic run done. results: new rule triggered only when backlog >50 AND tokens_per_req median > 3200. steady long-requests without queue growth did not fire alert. attaching logs to PR.

nora: reviewing PR. please add unit tests for alert_replay to assert historical false-positive reduction.

observability-bot: PR updated with tests and grafana panels. review requested: @ethan, @zara, @leo.

oncall-bot: handoff: @leo is now oncall (23:20 UTC). nora: please hand off status.

nora: handed off: maintenance MW-3301 active until 00:20 UTC, silence S-1984 active until 00:30 UTC. PR 934 in review (alerts + dashboard), synthetic and replay validated. follow-ups: TKT-6122 for job metadata, runbook snippet, explore dynamic limiter prototype.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED  model-runner CPU throttling reduced; mitigation applied. Incident marked resolved at 23:46 UTC. Incident ID INC-7890.

ethan: post-incident owners: observability: @nora, infra scaling/ingress: @ethan, product scheduling: @zara, follow-up engineering: @leo.

nora: postmortem draft will include timeline, root cause (accidental promotion of long-token test to prod), mitigations (ingress cap + autoscale), alert tuning changes, replay validation, and action items. target draft tomorrow EOD.

zara: follow-ups: 1) implement scheduled job metadata (TKT-6122), 2) ensure deploy pipelines refuse prod-tagging for test jobs unless `allow_prod=true`, 3) add one-click ingress cap to runbook UI.

observability-bot: NOTE: silences and maintenance windows must be timeboxed and validated. if silence S-1984 remains active past 00:30 UTC, oncall will be paged.

nora: thanks all. closing thread once postmortem draft posted. :thumbsup:
